name: Peak XV Partners
identity_check: Peak XV Partners at peakxv.com: a multi-stage VC that began in 2006 as Sequoia Capital India, later expanded into Southeast Asia, and became an independent firm named Peak XV when Sequoia Capital split its global business into separate entities in 2023 (About page; FAQ on the Sequoia India/SEA rebrand). Its seed programme Surge runs at surge.peakxv.com ('Surge is the way Peak XV does seed investing'). Confirmed by domain, the firm's own history and press calling it 'formerly Sequoia Capital India & SEA'. Not Sequoia Capital (US), which is a separate firm with its own record. The website is operated by Peak XV Partners Operations LLC (Legal page).

Its 2026 funds centre on AI alongside fintech and consumer. Seed runs through Surge: $500K–$5M, any sector, open architecture, no board seats. Leaders also cite deeptech, from semiconductors to space.

open_items: Per-fund sizes of the three 2026 funds (India Seed, India Venture, APAC) are not disclosed anywhere fetched; recorded as one combined $1.3B line. The existing Growth fund's uninvested balance is also undisclosed.
Surge is not a separately sized fund: the Surge FAQ says it is how Peak XV does seed investing, with up to $5M from Peak XV. No Surge fund line recorded.

No fund close in 2024: the 2024 event is the October 2024 downsizing of the 2022-vintage funds (see conflicts). Month of the 2022 announcement not confirmed on a fetched page (year only). Peak XV Anchor Fund (perpetual, Mar 2024): size and close not disclosed.

HQ city not stated on any fetched page. The site lists offices in the US, India, Singapore and UAE without addresses; the website operator is Peak XV Partners Operations LLC. hq_country IN rests on the firm's origin as Sequoia Capital India and TechCrunch saying India remains its largest market; confirm.

Flipped companies: no page states a policy on US-domiciled companies with Indian founders. Evidence only: the firm invests in the US (Blacksmith, Alex, Luminai) and in Indian companies (C2i, Bengaluru); the Surge application asks the country of registration without requiring one; Atomicwork has Indian founders and most customers in the US but its domicile is not stated.

No stated industrial / manufacturing / factory-AI focus. Closest signals: Ethereal Machines (CNC precision manufacturing, Series A Jun 2024; older than 24 months), C2i (AI data-centre power hardware), Zetwerk in the portfolio list, Puralink (underground pipe robots, Surge 12), and Rajan Anandan citing deeptech from semiconductors to space and battery recycling.

Partner sector focus is not stated on the team pages; only Rajan Anandan's deeptech remarks are recorded. Shailendra Singh co-leads seed with Anandan (Forbes India) and wrote the Luminai and Blacksmith posts; Arnav Sahu drives US investing; Abhishek Mohan was promoted to general partner in Feb 2026 (TechCrunch). Departed partners (Shailesh Lakhani, Abheek Anand, Harshjit Sethi, Ashish Agrawal, Ishaan Mittal, Tejeshwi Sharma) excluded.
Main fund (venture / growth) has no pitch form; the site gives only a general contact email. application_url and accepts_cold_inbound refer to Surge.
Ditto and Rosella round dates are only 'earlier this year' (2026) per TechCrunch; websites and HQs not stated. Rosella amount is 'roughly' $2.5M.
Kello, Round1 and Zoop (Impact AI PitchFest, Feb 2026): amounts and stages undisclosed. Memfold AI (same founders as Surge 12's Alma) and Companion Labs (consumer) from the same batch not recorded.
Blacksmith's $550M valuation not recorded: TechCrunch does not say pre- or post-money. Ringg: Peak XV is the only named investor in the $10M extension; lead not stated.
HQ not stated for Blacksmith, Luminai, Alex, TrueFoundry, Atomicwork, RapidCanvas (teams in India for TrueFoundry and Atomicwork per TechCrunch).

Not fetched: Livemint (Surge backing US, UK, Australia startups, Mar 2025) was blocked; Forbes (Arnav Sahu, Bay Area, Apr 2025) and YourStory (Nov 2025, Oct 2024) returned 403.
